message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that involves thousands of square meters of steel and concrete. In practice, the tower is repainted every 7–10 years as part of its routine maintenance program. A full repaint can take anywhere from **six to nine months** if you’re doing it in a single continuous effort, but the actual work is usually broken into phases:

| Phase | Typical Duration | What Happens |
|-------|------------------|--------------|
| **Preparation & Surface Cleaning** | 1–2 weeks | Removing old paint, rust, and debris; applying protective coatings. |
| **Primer Application** | 1–2 weeks | Applying a base coat to ensure adhesion of the final paint layers. |
| **Color Coating (multiple layers)** | 3–4 weeks | Applying the chosen color (often a special “Eiffel Tower Red” or “Parisian Bronze”) in several coats. |
| **Detail Work & Finishing Touches** | 1–2 weeks | Painting decorative elements, signage, and any custom finishes. |
| **Inspection & Final Touch‑ups** | 1–2 weeks | Quality checks, touch‑ups, and cleaning up the site. |

These phases are typically staggered so that workers can move from one section to another without having to wait for the entire tower to be finished. Because the tower is a public landmark, the work is scheduled during periods of low tourist traffic and often takes place over a summer season.

So, while a single continuous paint job might take around **six to nine months**, the overall project—including planning, permits, and phased execution—can span **one to two years** from start to finish.
